records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Reuben, firstborn of Israel, for he [was] the firstborn, but when he profaned [the] beds of his father was given his birthright to [the] sons of Joseph son of Israel, and not to be enrolled by genealogy according to the birthright;

en.L: And [the] sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel—for he [was] the firstborn, but when he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, and [one is] not to be enrolled in the genealogy according to the birthright;
en.B: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel—he was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright went to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, and the genealogy is not set out according to the birthright;
en.R: This is the family of Reuben, Israel's oldest son. Reuben was born first, but he slept with one of his father's wives and so brought shame on his father's bed. Because of this, his rights as the oldest son were given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel. So the family records are not set out by who had the rights of the oldest son.

es.L: Y [los] hijos de Rubén, el primogénito de Israel —porque él [era] el primogénito, pero cuando profanó el lecho de su padre, su primogenitura fue dada a los hijos de José hijo de Israel, y no [se ha de] inscribir en la genealogía según la primogenitura;
es.B: Los hijos de Rubén, el primogénito de Israel —él era el primogénito, pero como profanó el lecho de su padre, su primogenitura pasó a los hijos de José hijo de Israel, y la genealogía no se ordena según la primogenitura;
es.R: Esta es la familia de Rubén, el hijo mayor de Israel. Rubén nació primero, pero se acostó con una de las esposas de su padre y así deshonró el lecho de su padre. Por eso, sus derechos de hijo mayor fueron dados a los hijos de José hijo de Israel. Así que los registros familiares no se ordenan según quién tenía los derechos de hijo mayor.

fr.L: Et les fils de Ruben, le premier-né d’Israël — car il [était] le premier-né, mais quand il souilla le lit de son père, son droit d’aînesse fut donné aux fils de Joseph, fils d’Israël, et [on ne doit] pas être inscrit dans la généalogie selon le droit d’aînesse ;
fr.B: Les fils de Ruben, le premier-né d’Israël — il était le premier-né, mais parce qu’il avait souillé le lit de son père, son droit d’aînesse passa aux fils de Joseph, fils d’Israël, et la généalogie n’est pas établie selon le droit d’aînesse ;
fr.R: Voici la famille de Ruben, le fils aîné d’Israël. Ruben était né le premier, mais il a couché avec une des femmes de son père, et il a ainsi déshonoré le lit de son père. À cause de cela, ses droits de fils aîné ont été donnés aux fils de Joseph, fils d’Israël. C’est pourquoi les registres de familles ne sont pas classés selon les droits du fils aîné.

sw.L: Na wana wa Reubeni mzaliwa wa kwanza wa Israeli—kwa maana yeye [alikuwa] mzaliwa wa kwanza, lakini alipokinajisi kitanda cha baba yake, haki yake ya mzaliwa wa kwanza ilipewa wana wa Yusufu mwana wa Israeli, wala [mtu] hakuandikwa katika orodha ya ukoo kwa kufuata haki ya mzaliwa wa kwanza;
sw.B: Wana wa Reubeni mzaliwa wa kwanza wa Israeli—yeye alikuwa mzaliwa wa kwanza, lakini kwa sababu alikinajisi kitanda cha baba yake, haki yake ya mzaliwa wa kwanza ilipewa wana wa Yusufu mwana wa Israeli, na orodha ya ukoo haikupangwa kwa kufuata haki ya mzaliwa wa kwanza;
sw.R: Hii ndiyo jamaa ya Reubeni, mwana mkubwa wa Israeli. Reubeni alizaliwa wa kwanza, lakini alilala na mmoja wa wake wa baba yake, akaleta aibu juu ya kitanda cha baba yake. Kwa sababu hiyo, haki zake za mwana mkubwa zilipewa wana wa Yusufu mwana wa Israeli. Kwa hiyo kumbukumbu za jamaa hazikupangwa kwa kufuata nani alikuwa na haki za mwana mkubwa.

vi.L: Và các con trai của Ru-bên, con đầu lòng của Y-sơ-ra-ên—vì ông [là] con đầu lòng, nhưng khi ông làm ô uế giường của cha mình, quyền trưởng nam của ông đã được ban cho các con trai của Giô-sép con trai Y-sơ-ra-ên, và [người ta] không ghi vào gia phả theo quyền trưởng nam;
vi.B: Các con trai của Ru-bên, con đầu lòng của Y-sơ-ra-ên—ông là con đầu lòng, nhưng vì ông đã làm ô uế giường của cha mình, nên quyền trưởng nam của ông đã về tay các con trai của Giô-sép con trai Y-sơ-ra-ên, và gia phả không được sắp theo quyền trưởng nam;
vi.R: Đây là gia đình của Ru-bên, con trai cả của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ru-bên sinh ra trước hết, nhưng ông đã ăn nằm với một người vợ của cha mình và làm nhục giường của cha. Vì thế, quyền của con trai cả đã được trao cho các con trai của Giô-sép con trai Y-sơ-ra-ên. Cho nên gia phả không được sắp theo người có quyền trưởng nam.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘의 맏아들 르우벤의 아들들은—그는 맏아들이었으나 그가 자기 아버지의 침상을 더럽혔으므로 그의 맏아들의 권리가 이스라엘의 아들 요셉의 아들들에게 주어졌고, 맏아들의 권리에 따라 족보에 오르지 않았다.
ko.B: 이스라엘의 맏아들 르우벤의 아들들은—르우벤은 맏아들이었으나 아버지의 침상을 더럽혔기 때문에 그의 맏아들의 권리는 이스라엘의 아들 요셉의 아들들에게 넘어갔고, 족보도 맏아들의 권리에 따라 적히지 않았다.
ko.R: 이스라엘의 맏아들 르우벤의 집안은 이러하다. 르우벤은 맏이로 태어났지만, 아버지의 아내 가운데 하나와 잠자리를 같이하여 아버지의 침상을 욕되게 했다. 그래서 맏아들로서 그가 누릴 권리는 이스라엘의 아들 요셉의 아들들에게 넘어갔다. 그러므로 집안 기록은 누가 맏아들의 권리를 가졌는지에 따라 적히지 않았다.

decisions.choice: he defiled his father's bed: Reuben lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine
decisions.reason: This looks back to Genesis 35:22, where Reuben lay with Bilhah, and to Jacob's words in Genesis 49:4, which use the same verb "defile" and the same word for his father's bed. Jacob there took from Reuben the first place that was his by birth (49:3-4).

decisions.choice: the birthright given to the sons of Joseph: the firstborn's double share
decisions.reason: The firstborn received a double share of his father's inheritance (Deuteronomy 21:17). Jacob adopted Joseph's two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, as his own (Genesis 48:5), so Joseph's line received two tribal shares where every other son received one.

decisions.choice: not to be enrolled according to the birthright: the genealogy is not arranged by the birthright
alternatives: Reuben is not listed as firstborn
Joseph is not listed as firstborn
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has an infinitive with no stated subject: "and not to be enrolled according to the birthright". Read as impersonal, it explains why the genealogies do not put the holder of the birthright first: Judah, not Joseph, leads the lists (chapters 2-4), as verse 2 explains. It may instead mean that Reuben is not listed as firstborn, or that Joseph, though he had the birthright, is not listed as firstborn.

decisions.choice: the list breaks off for an explanation and resumes in verse 3
decisions.reason: After "the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel" the writer stops to explain why Reuben, though firstborn, does not come first in these genealogies. The explanation runs to the end of verse 2, and verse 3 starts the list again with the same words.

decisions.choice: dashes around the explanation
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced mark the break in the sentence with a dash here and at the end of verse 2 (m4). Readable makes the explanation into sentences of its own.

decisions.choice: slept with one of his father's wives and so brought shame on his father's bed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of defiling the bed refers to (m1). Bilhah was a secondary wife of Jacob (Genesis 30:4).

decisions.choice: dashes around the explanation (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced mark the break in the list with a dash (—) here and at the end of verse 2, as the English does (m4); Readable makes the explanation into sentences of its own.

decisions.choice: "primogenitura" (L, B); "derechos de hijo mayor" (R)
decisions.reason: The firstborn's rights keep the published Genesis 25 wording at Literal and Balanced ("derechos de primogénito" there in speech); Readable says "derechos de hijo mayor" in plain words.

decisions.choice: le droit d'aînesse (L, B); les droits de fils aîné (R)
decisions.reason: "Le droit d'aînesse" is the usual French term, known from Esau's story; Readable says it in plain words, as the English Readable "rights as the oldest son".

decisions.choice: haki ya mzaliwa wa kwanza (birthright)
decisions.reason: The birthright is the firstborn's right to the double share and the headship; "haki ya mzaliwa wa kwanza" says it plainly, and Readable "haki za mwana mkubwa".

decisions.choice: "quyền trưởng nam" (L, B); "quyền của con trai cả" (R)
decisions.reason: The word of the Vietnamese Genesis 25 and 27 for the birthright; Readable says it in plain words.

decisions.choice: dashes around the explanation
decisions.reason: As the English does, Literal and Balanced mark the break in the sentence with a dash here and at the end of verse 2; Readable makes the explanation sentences of its own.

decisions.choice: dashes around the explanation, the list resumed in verse 3
decisions.reason: As the English, Literal and Balanced keep the break in the sentence with a dash; the subject "르우벤의 아들들은" is taken up again in verse 3.

decisions.reason: A plain Korean phrase that a reader understands without a church word; it is kept at every level and in verse 2.

ko.L: 유다가 그의 형제들 가운데서 강해졌고 그에게서 통치자가 [나왔으나], 맏아들의 권리는 요셉의 것이었다—

decisions.choice: ruler (nagid): the leader chosen to rule God's people, here David and the kings after him
decisions.reason: Nagid is the word used when God appoints Saul and David to lead his people (1 Samuel 9:16; 13:14; 2 Samuel 7:8). David says that God chose Judah to be ruler and chose him from Judah (28:4).

decisions.choice: Judah grew strong among his brothers
decisions.reason: Jacob's blessing said Judah's brothers would bow to him and the scepter would not leave him (Genesis 49:8-10). Chronicles sees this fulfilled in the kings of David's line, which is why Judah heads the genealogies.

decisions.choice: but the birthright was Joseph's: rule and birthright went to different sons
decisions.reason: Reuben's firstborn rights were divided: the double share went to Joseph (verse 1), and the leadership to Judah.

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: As across Samuel, Kings and Chronicles, nagid is "ruler" at Literal and Balanced and "leader" at Readable.

decisions.choice: kiongozi
decisions.reason: *Nagid* is "kiongozi" at every level, as in the Swahili Samuel drafts.

decisions.choice: "người cai trị" (L, B); "người lãnh đạo" (R) for *nagid*
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms give "người lãnh đạo" for *nagid*; here, where the word is set beside Judah's strength among his brothers, Literal and Balanced say "người cai trị", as the English says "ruler" at those levels, and Readable keeps "người lãnh đạo".
